_about: Task lists and their status, shown on the Tasks page. Agents: see agents/REPO_PROTOCOL.md (update status and log, never the note field).

tasks.projectGoal: Rebuild ACC frontdoor register access in your own sandbox, using the existing ACC register model and the sideband-bus (SB) UVC, until you can explain every step. Planned 29 Oct to 2 Nov.
tasks.title: Day 1: trace the path and write the adapter
tasks.detail: Find which map frontdoor uses, its base address, and whether ACC sits inside a bigger SB or SoC map. Work out one read-write register's full address by hand, then find it in an SB log or waveform from your ACC_BE runs. Fill in the contract block in acc_sb_adapter.sv from the real SB item and driver, write reg2bus and bus2reg yourself, then compare with the team's adapter and explain every difference.
tasks.doneWhen: you can explain, without notes, how one REG.write() reaches the bus (Q5).

tasks.projectGoal: Rebuild ACC frontdoor register access in your own sandbox, using the existing ACC register model and the sideband-bus (SB) UVC, until you can explain every step. Planned 29 Oct to 2 Nov.
tasks.title: Day 2: connect it, then prediction
tasks.detail: Connect the map to the SB sequencer through your adapter. Choose how the mirror is updated: the register model from your own accesses, or a predictor on the SB monitor, and predict what happens with both on. Write a check sequence on one read-write, one read-only and one side-effect register (such as write-1-to-clear): write, read back, check the mirror.
tasks.doneWhen: you can explain how a read value gets back into the model and how the mirror stays in sync (Q6).

tasks.projectGoal: Rebuild ACC frontdoor register access in your own sandbox, using the existing ACC register model and the sideband-bus (SB) UVC, until you can explain every step. Planned 29 Oct to 2 Nov.
tasks.title: Day 3: frontdoor vs backdoor, then break it
tasks.detail: Experiments, predicting each result first: frontdoor write then backdoor peek; backdoor poke then frontdoor read; frontdoor write to the read-only register; reset values with uvm_reg_hw_reset_seq. Then inject one bug at a time and predict the symptom: wrong base address, swapped read/write in bus2reg, no set_sequencer call, provides_responses not matching the driver. Write each up as trigger, root cause, DUT or testbench, where the fix went.
tasks.doneWhen: you can answer Q7 (what frontdoor checks that backdoor skips) from your own results.

tasks.projectGoal: Two tasks a week: one thing to learn and one thing to do. A week counts once you can explain it back, not once you've read about it.
tasks.title: Week 1: coverage scores
tasks.detail: Learn group vs instance scores, union vs average modes, and code vs functional coverage. Do the Verdi re-check on one multi-instance covergroup, then write a short note for your team on what the sign-off number means.
tasks.doneWhen: you can explain it without the user guide open.
tasks.log: 28 Oct: union 75% and average 50% calculated, your flow's average mode found in Verdi, and "coverage records, it doesn't check" confirmed. Left: the sign-off sentence (see Open explain-back questions).

tasks.projectGoal: Two tasks a week: one thing to learn and one thing to do. A week counts once you can explain it back, not once you've read about it.
tasks.title: Week 2: your spec, first pass
tasks.detail: Learn how to read a spec: functional spec (what the design should do) vs MAS (how it's built), interface tables, register map, timing diagrams, state machines. Pick one block and write a one-page summary: purpose, interfaces, key registers, one transaction flow from start to end, three things that must be verified.
tasks.doneWhen: you can walk me through that transaction flow from memory.

tasks.projectGoal: Two tasks a week: one thing to learn and one thing to do. A week counts once you can explain it back, not once you've read about it.
tasks.title: Week 3: the Xcelium comparison
tasks.detail: Learn why the same seed gives different stimulus on different simulators, and what can fairly be compared. Rewrite the comparison criteria in your HTML migration guide around pass rate across a seed sweep, coverage closure and failure categories.
tasks.doneWhen: the revised checklist is in the guide.

tasks.projectGoal: Two tasks a week: one thing to learn and one thing to do. A week counts once you can explain it back, not once you've read about it.
tasks.title: Week 4: your flow and how it fails
tasks.detail: Learn the regression's stages from trigger to signature mail. Read the regression wrapper script yourself first, then use AI only to check your reading. Answer three failure paths: a crash before the limit is released, a cron overlap, and why vcs_run.log gets deleted. Propose one fix.
tasks.doneWhen: you've drawn the flow and written the three answers.

tasks.projectGoal: Two tasks a week: one thing to learn and one thing to do. A week counts once you can explain it back, not once you've read about it.
tasks.title: Week 5: practice testbench, phases and objections
tasks.detail: Learn UVM phasing and how objections start and end a test. Build the skeleton (FIFO DUT, test, env), then break it on purpose: never raise an objection, then never drop one, and read the logs each time.
tasks.doneWhen: you can predict both symptoms before running.

tasks.projectGoal: Two tasks a week: one thing to learn and one thing to do. A week counts once you can explain it back, not once you've read about it.
tasks.title: Week 6: spec to test scenarios
tasks.detail: Learn what makes a good test scenario: one behaviour, a clear expected result, how it's checked. Turn your Week 2 summary into a mini verification plan of 8 to 10 scenarios.
tasks.doneWhen: every scenario has an expected result.

tasks.title: Week 7: driver, sequencer, sequences
tasks.detail: Learn the handshake between driver and sequencer. Write the driver and two sequences for the practice testbench.
tasks.doneWhen: you can explain who waits for whom.

tasks.detail: Learn what crosses the DPI-C boundary and which side calls which. Trace this in your team's backdoor flow and write it up.
